newsitem.title: UK: Generic drug growth to outpace new products - study.
newsitem.headline: Generic drug growth to outpace new products - study.

text.p: Growth in sales of cheaper generic versions of drugs will outpace that of new pharmaceutical products over the next three years, management consultancy Datamonitor said on Monday.

In a study of the generics market, Datamonitor said it expected the generic market to grow by 14 per cent a year between now and the year 2000, compared with a rate of six percent for the innovative drug market.
Datamonitor said the world generic drug market was estimated to be worth between $30 billion and $40 billion in 1996.
It said cost pressures on healthcare providers were making cheaper generic products increasingly attractive, making them "one of the fastest-growing segments of the pharmaceutical industry."

The report said the generic share of the U.S. drugs market was expected to rise to 16 percent in 2000 from 11 percent in 1995. This would represent around 50 percent of the whole market in volume terms.
In Britain, the report predicted generic market share would rise to 24 percent from 15 percent and in Germany to 40 percent from 30 percent over the same period.

"Growth of generics is also certain to occur in less mature markets such as France, Italy and Japan...due to recent changes in regulation which have created a more environment for generic pharmaceuticals."

Datamonitor said that as generic drugs can command only a fraction of the prices paid for branded drugs, generic manufacturers had to ensure that products were launched as fast as possible after patents expired and in as many countries as possible.
"It is imperative that generics companies conduct their manufacturing and regulatory processes as efficiently as possible," the report added.
